title: NEW: Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international soccer. In an Instagram post showing a handwritten note in Spanish, Messi confirmed he's hanging up his cleats from Argentina's national team: "After all this time since the final, and after thinking about it a lot, I want to tell everyone that I'm retiring from the national team. It was a decision that hurt and still hurts deep inside, but I understand that this is the right moment," Messi started. He ended his letter stating, "Thank you God for making me Argentine… Vamos Argentina! I wrote these words on July 21, two days after the final. Today, after what happened with my dad, I'm even more convinced of this decision than before." Lionel Messi's father, Jorge Messi, passed away at the age of 68 on August 7, 2026, following a long health battle.
summary:
NEW:  Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international soccer.

In an Instagram post showing a handwritten note in Spanish, Messi confirmed he's hanging up his cleats from Argentina's national team:

"After all this time since the final, and after thinking about it a lot, I want to tell everyone that I'm retiring from the national team. It was a decision that hurt and still hurts deep inside, but I understand that this is the right moment," Messi started.

He ended his letter stating, "Thank you God for making me Argentine… Vamos Argentina! I wrote these words on July 21, two days after the final. Today, after what happened with my dad, I'm even more convinced of this decision than before."

Lionel Messi's father, Jorge Messi, passed away at the age of 68 on August 7, 2026, following a long health battle.
full_text:
NEW:  Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international soccer.

In an Instagram post showing a handwritten note in Spanish, Messi confirmed he's hanging up his cleats from Argentina's national team:

"After all this time since the final, and after thinking about it a lot, I want to tell everyone that I'm retiring from the national team. It was a decision that hurt and still hurts deep inside, but I understand that this is the right moment," Messi started.

He ended his letter stating, "Thank you God for making me Argentine… Vamos Argentina! I wrote these words on July 21, two days after the final. Today, after what happened with my dad, I'm even more convinced of this decision than before."

title: Some Patriots thoughts/news nuggets: 🏈This was a straight-forward cut-down day. No shocking moves. One of the more interesting decisions was keeping quarterback Behren Morton, the 2026 seventh-round pick from Texas Tech, as the third option. It speaks to the importance of the position; notable that four teams kept four QBs on initial 53-man rosters (Eagles, Falcons, Steelers, Vikings), which is unusual. 🏈Would be shocked if the Patriots don’t aggressively address OLB, either on the practice squad or a waiver claim. Teams aren’t giving quality pass-rushers away, but a player like Caleb Murphy – who played five games for the Patriots last season, was waived by the Giants, and would be a plug-and-play core special teamer at minimum – would provide the team with some much-needed experienced OLB depth. 🏈Five. That’s the number of players I believe would have been on the initial 53-man roster if not for injuries and it’s a reminder that when the topic of the Patriots’ lack of depth is broached, it is as much about health as it is shaky drafting. That list includes OT Marcus Bryant, TE Julian Hill, OLB Harold Landry III, RB Terrell Jennings and ST Brenden Schooler. 🏈Veteran punter Mitch Wishnowsky is a target for the Patriots with incumbent Bryce Baringer still sidelined due to an undisclosed lower-body injury. The expectation is Wishnowsky will be in town for a physical soon. Wouldn't surprise me if that moves quickly. 🏈NT Cory Durden was a waiver claim at this time last year and he has become an important cog for the team. One thing that has been apparent: Because the Patriots are No. 31 in the waiver-claim order this year, instead of No. 4 last year, they’ve been more aggressive with trades for RB Corey Kiner (Cardinals) and T/G Walter Rouse (Vikings) to fill depth roles. So Kiner is the early leading candidate to be this year's Durden. 🏈On Rouse (6-6, 330), he was a tackle up until training camp this year, when the Vikings began experimenting with him at guard. He falls into the Bill Parcells category of “looks good coming off the bus” player. Rouse, who played at Stanford and Oklahoma and entered the NFL as a 2024 sixth-round pick of the Vikings, has said he hopes to be a doctor.

title: Here are 10 thoughts on the Commanders' initial 53-man roster: 1) It's obvious that Fabian Moreau is going to be back on the team as soon as Trey Amos hits IR. WSH only has three healthy CB's on the 53 until Moreau is brought back, but he's vested and doesn't need to clear waivers so he isn't at risk of being claimed. 2) Speaking of Amos -- the IR news is bad. That means he's going to miss 4 games. That's your CB1 in a fairly pedestrian CB room. What is going on with Amos? Putting him on IR is an indicator that he's still weeks away from practicing at game speed. How did we get here? 3) The center position continues to flummox me. Julian Good-Jones went from "competing for the starting spot" to cut in the span of a few weeks. Matt Gulbin went from a rough joint practice against Baltimore to the only healthy guy on the team at the position in days. Clearly Nick Allegretti is due back soon but I'm stunned a veteran hasn't been added yet. That will undoubtedly happen tomorrow. 4) Athan Kaliakmanis as QB3 is a clear endorsement of how well he played in the preseason, namely against Detroit. He showed a little too much for the Commanders to feel like they could get him on the practice squad. My guess is they could have gotten him to the taxi group but they were not willing to risk it. 5) The 7th WR spot came down to Luke McCaffrey and Van Jefferson. I like the decision to keep McCaffrey even though Jefferson is the better WR right now. So why keep Luke? Well he's younger, has more upside, helps on special teams and is under contract for longer. WSH already has several WR's on expiring deals (Diggs, Burks, Brown) and Terry McLaurin may even be in his final year with the team pending the results of the 2026 campaign. It makes sense to layer the roster with more players who have more term remaining like McCaffrey. 6) The DT spot ended up being super deep and very competitive. I thought Byron Cowart and Maurice Hurst were both good enough to make the squad. Same with Shy Tuttle, although I think he'll rejoin the team as soon as Johnny Newton hits IR. Like Moreau, he's vested and doesn't need to go through the waivers process. I think the Commanders are well put on the interior up front. 7) Speaking of roster spots I like -- I really think Adam Peters did a nice job with the edge, off-ball linebacker, tight end and wide receiver spots. 8) I'm surprised Ale Kaho got cut. I would have kept him on the 53 as a 6th LB. He is good on special teams and he could've helped Kain Medrano and Jordan Magee as anchors on teams and depth backers. He'll likely end up on the practice squad and stay in the building. 9) The CB room gives me anxiety. Mike Sainristil needs to have a much better season than he did last year. With Amos out, Sainristil will be counted on to help anchor the position on the outside. The Cowboys loom in Week 2 and that meeting with George Pickens and Ceedee Lamb is going to be a massive test for WSH's pass rush. They'll need to protect the corner room. 10) Speaking of the Commanders' pass rush, Odafe Oweh and K'Lavon Chaisson have both been battling injuries and haven't practiced in weeks. The Commanders defense has a chance to be massively improved but only if those two guys can be healthy and prolific.

3) The center position continues to flummox me. Julian Good-Jones went from "competing for the starting spot" to cut in the span of a few weeks. Matt Gulbin went from a rough joint practice against Baltimore to the only healthy guy on the team at the position in days. Clearly Nick Allegretti is due back soon but I'm stunned a veteran hasn't been added yet. That will undoubtedly happen tomorrow.

He showed a little too much for the Commanders to feel like they could get him on the practice squad. My guess is they could have gotten him to the taxi group but they were not willing to risk it.

5) The 7th WR spot came down to Luke McCaffrey and Van Jefferson. I like the decision to keep McCaffrey even though Jefferson is the better WR right now. So why keep Luke? Well he's younger, has more upside, helps on special teams and is under contract for longer. WSH already has several WR's on expiring deals (Diggs, Burks, Brown) and Terry McLaurin may even be in his final year with the team pending the results of the 2026 campaign. It makes sense to layer the roster with more players who have more term remaining like McCaffrey. 

6) The DT spot ended up being super deep and very competitive. I thought Byron Cowart and Maurice Hurst were both good enough to make the squad. Same with Shy Tuttle, although I think he'll rejoin the team as soon as Johnny Newton hits IR. Like Moreau, he's vested and doesn't need to go through the waivers process. I think the Commanders are well put on the interior up front. 

7) Speaking of roster spots I like -- I really think Adam Peters did a nice job with the edge, off-ball linebacker, tight end and wide receiver spots.

title: Not such big surprises on the Chiefs’ 53, but a few things that caught my attention: 1) Moving on from Emari Demercado speaks to a couple things: the Chiefs see Ken Walker as a three-down back, and they love what Emmett Johnson has showed. Brashard Smith is a wild card Andy Reid can move around on offense, and he’s KR2. Best return in a while for KC on Friday night. 2) Cutting Andrew Armstrong means the Chiefs think he can pass through waivers, which is possible. Remember this is a second-year player, not a rookie. It also speaks to Nikko Remigio, who Dave Toub trusts better than anyone on the roster to catch a punt. The Chiefs have played in 22 one-score games the past two years alone. Even one muff matters. We’ll see on Armstrong. 3) Esa Pole was cut, and here I’d echo the Armstrong point — I think he probably gets to the practice squad. From posts (tweets, whatever), it seems like fans are out on Pole, anyway, but a lot of the same fans were upset when Pole was claimed last year (NYJ). 4) The Chiefs kept seven cornerbacks. Like Remigio, Toub values Kevin Knowles, who is a four-phase special-teamer. That matters. The Chiefs have never kept 11 defensive backs since Spags took over (2019), but that’s where L’Jarius Sneed fits in. The health is always in question. 3 waiver priorities in order for me: LB, OT, DE

title: Some leftover thoughts on the #49ers' initial 53-man roster: - No real surprises anywhere. So much was dictated by injury issues that are in varying lengths and degrees. There's obviously still going to be a lot of juggling so Niners can get players they want to use this year through to injured reserve tomorrow without having to decide right away whether they'll be back. Remember, players who go on IR after cutdown day don't have to be designated to return until they're ready to begin practicing. - On that note, a handful of names of guys on the current roster to keep an eye on as potentially landing on IR on Monday: DB Nate Hobbs (groin), LB Nick Martin (hamstring) Others who were injured recently and we don't know their status: CB Ephesians Prysock (shoulder), TE Brayden Willis (concussion) We also don't really know how far along S Malik Mustapha (hamstring), OT Vederian Lowe (high ankle) and LB Luke Gifford (hamstring) are right now. Have seen all working on the side but unclear exactly where they are in process. Also, G Dominick Puni returned from a concussion then had residual issues and missed practice last week. Don't know where he stands. All of this is more difficult because Niners have to leave in a few days for Australia. So, they have to do some projecting on this and obviously won't want guys with certain injuries on such a long haul flight. - P Corliss Waitman and LS Jon Weeks will be back. Much like they did with P Thomas Morstead last year, this is a pair of vested vets who don't have to clear waivers, so they can be brought back after getting some of the aforementioned guys to injured reserve. - The trade for OL Jarrett Patterson is official per the transaction wire so the Niners will plug him into the 53rd spot on the roster. Patterson has started 7 career regular season games at center and 14 at guard (all on the left side, FWIW). At minimum, this is a replacement for Brett Toth, who landed on IR, and at maximum it's another option for the LG job. - It appears that Connor Colby beat out Robert Jones for a guard spot but it's fair to wonder if Jones could still return. He's a vested veteran who is still coming back from a calf injury. Once he's healed, could those two swap? Could one potentially land on the practice squad? Doesn't feel like we've seen the end of the left guard shuffle. - Some guys Kyle Shanahan has said he hopes to have back at practice in some form this week: DE Nick Bosa, QB Kurtis Rourke, CB Upton Stout. 2004: PR/KR B.J. Sams
2005: S B.J. Ward
2006: RB Cory Ross
2007: OLB Edgar Jones
2008: ILB Jameel McClain
2009: ILB Dannell Ellerbe
2010: LS Morgan Cox
2011: WR LaQuan Williams
2012: K Justin Tucker
2013: WR Marlon Brown, S Brynden Trawick
2014: ILB Zach Orr, OT James Hurst
2015: RB Terrence Magee
2016: NT Michael Pierce
2017: FB Patrick Ricard, CB Jaylen Hill, ILB Bam Bradley
2018: CB Darius Williams, ILB Chris Board, WR Janarion Grant
2019: OL Patrick Mekari, ILB Otaro Alaka
2020: No undrafted rookies made initial 53
2021: S Ar’Darius Washington
2022: ILB Josh Ross
2023: RB Keaton Mitchell, OLB Malik Hamm
2024: S Beau Brade
2025: CB Keyon Martin, S Reuben Lowery, ILB Jay Higgins
2026: QB Joe Fagnano, OLB Ethan Burke

Of these undrafted rookies, four went on to become All-Pros: Morgan Cox, Justin Tucker, Zach Orr and Patrick Ricard.
author: Jamison Hensley (@jamisonhensley)

title: QB Joe Fagnano and OLB Ethan Burke both made the Ravens' final cutdown, which continues a remarkable trend. The Ravens have had at least one undrafted rookie make their initial 53-man roster in 22 of the last 23 years. This also continues great stories for Fagnano and Burke. Fagnano wasn’t part of the Ravens’ original undrafted rookie class and signed with Baltimore just before rookie minicamp. He moved up to No. 3 QB after Skyler Thompson was placed on IR on Aug. 12 and earned a roster spot with a strong preseason. Burke grew up in Baltimore and was once a high-profile lacrosse recruit. His outstanding play in the preseason — four tackles, one sack, two QB hits and 2 forced fumbles — forced Baltimore to make room for him on its roster.

title: QUICK THOUGHT: I recall one time Odell Beckham Jr. shared a video with me from his private workout in Arizona for NFL teams as he attempted to show he was back a year after tearing his ACL in Super Bowl 56 with the Rams. I looked at the video and I saw he had more confidence, but I also could see his vintage second-level gear was not there, just yet; and I actually told him that. I know what it looks like because I’ve seen it so many times covering him before; plus, Track people have an eye for those things. After that, Odell battled with some injuries, the depth of which he hasn’t fully disclosed publicly, but I’ll say I always knew, before he returned to the Giants today, that his injury setbacks had been a considerable factor before in his previous stops, as was his utilization and some unfulfilled promises….. Fast forward to this year, I attended one #Giants mandatory camp practice back in June to visit the team and to get a feel for where things were at. I didn’t have to be there long to have my eyes confirm what Beckham Jr. already told me several times before. I mentioned a number of times OBJ told me he was getting his legs back. As I mentally comparing the sights before me, to that day of his workout in Arizona, I knew I saw something different in his movement. The movement that comes from better physical and personal alignment; from one’s purpose changing. Quite simply, I saw flashes of his overall bounce again. A lot of that is physical healing. The most defining difference is clearer headspace; the lift you get from internally knowing you’ve weathered the storm. It’s been a long road since his rookie year, but there is nothing like the feeling one gets from persevering from disappointments and just life overall. OBJ returns to New York now as a Super Bowl champion, a father, and in the official Giants uniform once more. Most importantly, I know he’s most glad he’s received the opportunity to show that to his son, whilst seeing how the future unfolds. Always 13 in New York. #Giants.
